messages:
mira: Heads-up: canary publish for py/ts SDK 0.9.0 failed during the signing step. I'm stopping the pipeline. full log: 

```
publish-bot ERROR: signature verification failed
expected: SHA256:aaa111... actual: SHA256:bbb222...
gpg: WARNING: secret key 0xD4E5F6 not available
```

first_message_ts=1742101111

deploy-bot: Build 0.9.0-canary.7 failed at publish (exit 1). CI run: https://ci.internal/runs/1742101111

sam: Ack. Anyone who pushed recently? Could be a rotated key in local devs or CI secrets.

josh: I checked npm registry metadata: a manual publish for @redwood/sdk@0.9.0-canary landed this morning from a different CI runner. Registry shows uploader id mismatch.

elaine: Important: we must not re-use the same version with different signatures. That will create two distinct artifacts which is a nightmare for reproducibility.

mira: Agreed. I'm reverting the canary tag to the last verified build and pausing the GA window. I'll also open a short incident if this blocks >30m.

deploy-bot: Action: 0.9.0-canary -> SHA@77aabb restored (user=mira).

ben: Proposed next steps: 1) pin docs to last-stable; 2) validate CI GPG key fingerprint vs local key; 3) publish a patched canary (0.9.1-canary) once keys align.

sasha: We have a scheduled change window in ~2h. If we can't get a clean canary by then, we need rollback guidance for Dedicated customers and a small comms note for early adopters. Do not announce deprecations during this.

mira: Running a quick fingerprint audit now. If CI secret refers to key id 0xA1B2C3 but the successful manual publish used 0xD4E5F6, we need to contact the developer who did that publish.

josh: For npm we can retag dist-tags (`npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.9.0-canary stable` etc.) but PyPI doesn't let us reassign an existing release. For Python we'll likely need to publish a 0.9.1 build or append a build tag.

elaine: Release notes: keep a short neutral blurb about paused canary and advise pinning to stable. Keep deprecation messaging separate and scheduled for GA.

mira: Infra says CI secret fingerprint is currently 0xA1B2C3. Local dev key used in the manual publish is 0xD4E5F6. Opening P0 with infra to rotate or sync secrets. ETA 20m.

infra: Confirmed: CI secret mismatched. Rotating secret now and updating GitHub Actions. Will post new fingerprint when done.

ben: While infra rotates, add a pre-publish gate in CI to compare `GPG_EXPECTED_FPR` env with `gpg --with-colons --fingerprint` output. Fail early if mismatch. Small PR should do it.

mira: Good call. I'll draft the gate PR. Also, we should avoid any manual publishes until CI secrets verified.

josh: If someone manually published with a different key, that artifact should be treated as untrusted. For npm we can unpublish the canary tag; for PyPI we might need to file a registry support request to remove the conflicting file or to advise next steps.

sam: Docs action: pin sample install commands to `@redwood/sdk@stable` and `pip install redwood-sdk==0.8.4` in the quickstart until this is resolved. I can push that.

mira: Update: infra rotated and pushed new secret. New CI key fingerprint: 0xD4E5F6 (matches the local successful dev key). I've queued 0.9.1-canary build to staging registries first.

deploy-bot: 0.9.1-canary queued: jobs[build,test,staging-publish].

josh: After staging publish, please verify artifact checksums against CI artifacts and confirm signatures before promoting dist-tags. Use `sha256sum` and `gpg --verify`.

mira: Staging publish OK for both npm and PyPI staging. Checksums and signatures verified. Ready to promote to canary.

ben: Approve promote. Also add a short changelog entry and the neutral blurb for #incidents. I'll draft the blurb: 
"We paused the 0.9.0 canary after a signature mismatch was detected between CI and a recently published artifact. The canary tag was reverted to a verified build. We are validating signing keys and have queued 0.9.1-canary to staging. Please pin to stable until we confirm GA."

mira: I'll post that to #incidents and update the release checklist. Also keeping the deprecation note in a separate branch to avoid mixing messages.

sasha: I'll keep the change window open for 30m. If no regressions, we can proceed with GA. If anything odd, we abort and run the rollback playbook.

deploy-bot: Runbook check: create incident if publish outage > 1h. (auto)

mira: Final: promote done. npm dist-tag updated, PyPI new build uploaded as 0.9.1.post1 to avoid version conflict, docs pinned, fingerprint-gate PR opened: https://git.internal/pulls/1234

sam: Thanks all. Follow-up: add a short internal note listing who is allowed to do manual publishes and update the publishing runbook.

mira: Will do. Closing the thread once the postmortem draft is in. last_message_ts=1742104812
